STUDYLAB / LEARNING MODULES

Built to make the logic clearer.

About the course

StudyLab (formerly LogicLab) is an independent supplementary learning platform by Lefa Malatji. Its Programming Logic and Design content follows the five-unit outline supplied for this project. Explanations and practice questions are original; the platform is not an official institutional course or assessment.

Language and review

This first release is in English. Reviewed Sepedi explanations and additional modules are planned. Teaching content and diagram behaviour should be reviewed before use in assessed work.

Your progress and privacy

Lesson completion tracking is available in My progress. Earlier saved completion marks are retained. Pass the required lesson checks, then mark the lesson complete. Written practice tasks are self-checked against model solutions. The interactive exercises check selected answers and statement order, with two progressive hints and worked solutions unlocked after an attempt. Lesson answers, interactive-exercise progress, written drafts and editor code save in localStorage in this browser when available. Diagrams are generated locally. Tracer runtime inputs and execution history stay in page memory. Practice exam answers and self-assessed written marks save in this browser. A timed exam keeps its deadline when you leave the page; saved answers are submitted when the exam is open or next reopened after the deadline. Practice exams reuse the lesson quiz bank and are not secure assessments. Saved work does not sync across devices or identify individual students sharing one browser profile. Use Saved work to clear drafts and question progress on a shared device.

Practice, not secure assessment

Solutions are hidden in the interface until a complete attempt is submitted. Because this is a browser-only application, a determined user can inspect downloaded source files to find answers. It is not a secure examination system.

Current boundaries

The diagram lab supports a documented subset, not every pseudocode dialect. It validates structure but does not prove an algorithm correct. The interactive tracer runs documented variable, one-dimensional array and two-dimensional grid statements with typed input and execution limits. Guided array and sorting traces use fixed examples. Methods and classes are not executable in the tracer yet. The SQL workspace executes SQLite locally with documented SQL Server, PostgreSQL and MySQL compatibility modes. It is not a full native server. Demo database changes are temporary; SQL drafts and challenge feedback save in this browser. Check my answer compares challenge results against fresh demo and edge-case data; native SQL Server scripts and written explanations remain self-assessed. There are no student accounts, lecturer dashboards or cross-device progress in this version.
